 October 24, 2026

 Transport Evolved 
 On this week’s episode of TEN – Transport Evolved News! 
 Ford adds a gravel-ready Mustang Mach-E Trail, the Volkswagen Group recalls about 72,700 EVs worldwide over battery cells that could overheat, and T&E finds plug-in hybrids emit around six times their official CO₂ figures.
 These stories and more, on today’s show!

 Read the script here: 
 Today’s show is sponsored by the Electric Vehicle Association. Join up to support the electrification of transport today. And by Little Collie Shepherd! Meet the tool that handles abusive comments so you don’t have to! And by You – Stick around to find out how to keep us 100% independent!
 Welcome back to another episode of TEN — Transport Evolved News. Thanks for joining me. I hope that you are safe, well, and feel loved.
 We have a lot of news this week, so let’s get straight into today’s first story: the GM Forward event held this week in New York.
 The event is designed to give a glimpse into the automaker’s future, and this year, it leaned heavily into software-defined vehicles, AI assistants, autonomous technology, and a new next-generation EV platform. Officially GM’s fourth-generation since it started remaking EVs a decade ago, it promises 30% less wiring than today’s models, 40 times more processing power, and a lighter, smaller battery pack built using prismatic LMR battery cells. LMR stands for Lithium Manganese-Rich – a chemistry that GM says can offer up to 33% more energy density than LFP. It’s worth noting that various studies suggest LMR has its own weaknesses against NMC. As always, it’s a trade-off. GM hasn’t said when the new fourth-gen EVs will debut.
 This next story would normally be in our recall reminders, but it’s grown so much it deserves its own main story: a massive global recall of Volkswagen Group EVs.
 As we’ve covered in previous weeks, the Volkswagen Group has been planning a recall for some time. Now it’s official: 72,700 ID.3, ID.4, ID.7, ID. Buzz and Cupra Born models are affected. In an eerily familiar, similar fault to the one that plagued the Chevrolet Bolt EV and Hyundai Kona EV six years ago, Volkswagen notes potential production defects in some battery cells which, in extreme cases, could lead to fire, but hasn’t said which manufacturer is at fault. Volkswagen is sending OTA updates to stop affected vehicles charging beyond 80%. This issue is separate from a U.S. recall of cells made by SK Battery America. There, Volkswagen will also limit charging temporarily to 80% – but told owners they could decline.
 For several years now, European non-profit Transport & and Environment has been examining real-world emissions of plug-in hybrids, and how they differ from official lab tests.
 It’s just published its most recent report, noting that, yet again, emissions from plug-in hybrids are worsening in the real world, driven by a growth in popularity of larger PHEV models. It says PHEV models registered in 2024 in Europe emitted around six times their official CO₂ figures, up from five times in 2023. The difference adds around €680 euro a year in extra fuel costs for drivers. T&E’s proposed solution is a call on European legislators to keep soon-to-launch PHEV CO₂ accounting rules that are already getting push-back from Germany, and a proposal to limit PHEV fuel tank sizes to 15 litres or less for incentive eligibility. It also wants motor power to be three times the power output of the vehicle’s engine.
 For many years, Tesla has been viewed by some as being at the forefront of automotive development and innovation. Initially, that was well-earned.
 But as a just-published ranking for 2026 from the Center of Automotive Management shows, Tesla has dropped off the list of the top 10 most innovative EV brands, dropping from sixth place last time to eleventh. This year’s list sees Geely, Volkswagen and BYD in the top three places, with Mercedes-Benz in fourth, followed by BMW, SAIC, Hyundai-Kia, Renault, GM and Stellantis. The list tracks everything from vehicle to system innovations, as well as battery efficiency, charging, and drivetrain improvements. Ford, Xpeng, Nio and Toyota occupy positions 12 through 15, just below Tesla.
 Ahead of the official launch of the BMW iX5 in the U.S., the automaker has updated its expected EPA rating for the same.
 Like some of BMW’s other new models, the iX5 is a sibling to an internal combustion model – the X5 – and will eventually come in hydrogen fuel cell too. For the EV variant, the iX5 is built around Neue Klasse components, one of the reasons it’s exceeded its original range estimates. BMW originally promised an EPA range of 435 miles (700 kilometers) – but now that’s been increased to 450 miles (724 kilometers). While BMW hasn’t said how it increased range, I’d guess the launch of other Neue-Klasse powered models helped the iX5’s team tweak efficiency. Interestingly BMW’s pretty frank about the fact that customers stop worrying about range anxiety when 400 miles is achievable.
 Earlier this year, Mercedes-Benz released its AMG GT 4-Door Coupé in all-electric guise.
 Now the performance division has released a sibling, the AMG GT SUV. Built around the same truly bonkers performance AMG.EA platform as the AMG GT, the AMG GT SUV packs supercar performance into a full-sized SUV body. It has three times, and a zero to two hundred kilometer time in 7.2 seconds. It can charge at up to seven hundred and ten kilowatts thanks to its 800 volt battery pack, adding four hundred and fifty kilometers or two hundred and eighty miles) of WLTP range in 10 minutes, less time than it takes to pee and grab a coffee. It’ll be out of reach for most, me included, but it’s certainly a halo car to grab attention.
 It’s no secret that automakers in Europe and the U.S. are running scared from Chinese rivals and their super-fast, iterative development processes.
 But there’s another reason Chinese automakers scare legacy brands: the cost at which they can build cars – and AlixPartners laid that out in a new report. According to the group, Chinese EVs cost around 35% percent less on average to build than the same vehicle made in Europe, thanks to a supply chain that’s built around new vehicle tech. That’s something legacy brands in Europe and the U.S. just can’t compete against. And that’s compounded by a new survey from Canada, where 42% percent of likely EV buyers polled said they’d rather wait for Chinese-made EVs than buy a US-market one. Further, twice as many preferred a European-style market over a US one. The market is shifting, and I have no sympathy for the U.S. on this one. Politics matter, people.
 Earlier this year, the U.S. state of New Jersey enacted what many are calling one of the most draconian e-Bike laws in the entire country.
 Not only did it require all e-Bikes be registered and set tough rules about who could ride them – license required – but it also added arduous insurance requirements that have killed most e-bike sales and use. The rules, ostensibly designed to tackle safety and over-powered electric motorcycles masquerading as e-Bikes, were heavy-handed, sweeping up class 1, 2 and three e-bikes as well. Now, the state is looking to rescind some of its requirements by exempting the lowest speed e-Bikes – Class 1 and 2 from its regulations. This would make it legal again for people to ride Class 1 and 2 e-bikes without needing that extra paperwork. So we’ll keep our eyes on this one as it makes its way through the legislature.
 When Ford launched its range-topping Mustang Mach-E Rally a few years ago, I was all over it.
 Some of that might have been that its launch event involved going to DirtFish in Washington to razz it on a rally course – yes, that is me driving – but part of that was that it drove so darned well, mixing Mach-E GT power with extra ground clearance and rally mode. People wanted that extra ground clearance and wheels – but with less power, and price, so Ford’s obliged. Enter the Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail – a new variant with increased suspension height and rally-style wheels, built for adventure. Ford sells an optional roof bar on its accessory site for these cars for those feeling adventurous, and the Trail comes with Ford’s Pro Power mains inverter as standard – something Ford offers on some trims as an optional extra. I’ve already asked Ford for a press loaner, so watch this space!
 In the last few months, this position in the show has, unfortunately, often been filled by stories about the damage being done by the U.S.’ current policies and attitudes towards a cleaner greener future.
 But this week, while the story is about the U.S., it’s a good news story. See, thanks to the U.S. war in Iran – and the White House’s decision court Vladimir Putin, with one Government official this week calling him a humanitarian – the price of oil is causing more people to dump the pump for good. And with reduced EV choice thanks to policy decisions, people are looking to the used market. Cox Automotive just published its September 2026 EV Market Monitor, and it shows that while new EV sales fell 40.7% year over year, used EV sales roved twenty one point two percent, leading to one of the strongest used EV marketplaces we’ve seen. Combine that with more EVs coming off-lease, and there’s never been a better time to go electric with a pre-loved EV!
 Our Recall Reminders are coming next, but first, a sponsor message from Little Collie Shepherd!

And if you’re a creator who gets targeted for who you are or what you do, that can make life really tough.
 That’s where Little Collie Shepherd comes in. It reads your comments section and helps you deal with trolls and bots quickly and without the stress. Abuse is removed while honest, good-faith disagreement stays up – and if it isn’t sure, it holds the comment so you can review it yourself at an appropriate time.
 It won’t reply or write posts for you. It won’t automatically remove comments that don’t match the custom filters you set. And it doesn’t use your data for nefarious purposes.

You can sign up for a free trial, or find out more information by following the link in the show notes – or by pointing your mobile device at the on-screen QR code!
 And in the interests of full disclosure: Little Collie is owned by my wife, Kate, who came up with and wrote the whole app into response of some of the hate, threats and harassment we get on this channel. It is early days – so if you know someone who would benefit from Shepherd’s skills please spread the word. You’d be helping a lot. But also to the trolls? If it wasn’t for you, this app wouldn’t exist so… thank you?
 And now it’s time for our Recall Reminders. As usual, you’ll find links to the recalls in our show notes.
 New Flyer – and its sister company MCI – have recalled nearly 1,400 buses and coaches – including EVs – to address a hazard-indicator fault. Operators will be notified.
 Toyota has recalled its 2026 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid over a motor-generator ECU fault that could cause power. Dealers will update the ECU to fix the issue.
 Honda is recalling some of its hybrid models and its CR-V e:FCEV plug-in hybrid fuel cell EV over a fault with its tyre repair kit bottle cap. The cap can become a projectile.
 And finally for the recalls, the Volvo EX30 and its Cross Country sibling are being recalled in the U.S. due to a head restraint cushion that may detach in a crash.
 And those were your Recall Reminders! Now it’s time for our News Shorts. As usual, you’ll find full links on our website at transportevolved.com.
 Suzuki has officially priced its e SKY kei car in Japan, its first electric kei model. It will go on sale mid-November from 2.12 million yen, undercutting rivals from BYD and Honda.
 Citroën has added another concept vehicle to its lineup, the 2 CV Fourgonnette Concept. Debuted at the Paris Motor Show, the van variant teases an unconfirmed load-carrier.
 Vingroup’s Green SM has spent 2026 launching new all-electric taxi services across the world. Now it’s entered into the North American market with a Los Angeles launch.
 France and Germany have both proposed cutting CO₂ emission targets for 2035 from 100% to 90%, following heavy lobbying by the auto industry. The EU Parliament is debating the matter.
 Opel has announced the launch of a new entry-level variant for its Astra Electric and Astra Sports Tourer Electric. Called the “Start”, it will debut from just under €36,500. Euro.
 Cupra in the UK has launched a new entry-level trim spec for its Tavascan family, with a 58 kWh battery pack. It’s available in the UK from £39,995 on the road.
 As we previewed a few weeks back, FAW, Toyota, and GAC have signed a new framework agreement that sees GAC gain a 50% stake in FAW Toyota in China.
 Following pressure from the auto industry, the UK government is reviewing its ZEV mandate ahead of a potential relaxation of its EV sales targets between now and 2035.
 Stellantis and its Chinese partner Leapmotor have officially begun production of the B10 electric car in Zaragoza, Spain, bringing Leapmotor EV production back to Europe.
 BYD is expanding sales of its Racco EV in two new markets, with sales starting in Sri Lanka and soon to follow in Macao. Both markets have suffered as a result of rising oil prices.
 Saft has officially started production of solid-state battery cells in France, the first time solid-state cells have been in series production in the country. They will be used in aircraft.
 The Obrist Group, which made a name for itself by de-evolving Teslas and giving them internal combustion engines, has declared bankruptcy. It was nearly €32 million in debt.
 California’s MyFirstEV rebate program has already helped nearly 12,000 residents make the switch to an electric car. The program offers three and a half thousand dollars off sticker on a new EV.
 Zenobē and ComfortDelGro Australia are working on building what will be the largest electric bus depot in the West of Melbourne. When complete it will charge 130 buses.
 Mazda has launched its Mazda CX-6e in Thailand. The car based on the already in-production Mazda EZ-60, which has been on sale in China since late 2025. Is already gaining attention.
 A new report from Nikkei suggests Toyota plans to build its next-generation Corolla, including an all-electric version, at FAW Toyota in China from 2028. Toyota has yet to confirm this.
 Subaru, like many automakers, no longer seems interested in going all-electric in the U.S. But this week we learned it’s planning on phasing out ICE models in Europe by 2028.
 Fastned has posted its Q3 revenue, posting an increase in revenue of 63% percent year-over-year, a 43% percent increase in renewable energy delivered, and a 39% percent increase in charging sessions.
 Hon Hai Precision Industry – better known as Foxconn – has signed a final agreement to buy 50% percent of Mitsubishi Electric Mobility, Mitsubishi Electric’s automotive equipment business, for about ¥115 billion. Yen.
 At the Paris Motor Show, Fiat’s boss confirmed it’s preparing a new Panda family model, built on the same small EV platform as Citroën’s upcoming 2 CV.
 First Bus Norfolk is announcing its fleet now has 100 electric buses. The majority are in service in Norwich, so you can go down the city on an EV!
 Staying with UK bus fleets, the Greater Manchester bus fleet now has more than 500 electric buses on its fleet following its latest delivery of buses from Wrightbus.
 And not to be left out, the Hochbahn in Hamburg has begun trial operations of its first all-electric depot. It will ultimately be home to 130 electric buses.
 Hydrovolt, working with the Icelandic Recycling Fund, will soon collect end-of-life EV batteries in Iceland and recycle them at its plant in Norway, ensuring safe battery disposal.
 Bpost in Belgium has just celebrated passing a 40% percent milestone on its way to an electric fleet. By the end of October, 42% percent of its delivery vans will be all-electric.
 A new research project called CREED, led by Virtual Vehicle, has launched. Its goal is to research how EVs and heat pumps can help, not hinder, the electrical grid.
 BYD Malaysia has chosen Inokom, a Sime Motors subsidiary in Kulim, as its local assembly partner for BYD EVs in the nation. It’s the same plant that builds BMWs.
 England has removed planning permission requirements for EV owners wanting to install cross-pavement EV charging solutions for their cars. Local council approval is however, still needed.
 Porsche has made optional wireless charging available to order on its Cayenne Electric in Germany and other European markets. The feature was first shown at IAA last year.
 Reuters reported this week that Volkswagen’s partnership with Xpeng is not yielding the sales volume hoped. Data from China shows that the ID. UNYX 08, jointly developed, is selling poorly.
 As Rivian rolls out its autonomous driving software for point-to-point driving, its early access program is now accepting invite-only participants. They must sign an NDA.
 Kia has launched a remote-driven car-sharing pilot in South Korea using its PV5 EV. The vehicle is driven remotely to the renter’s location, then hands over control.
 Two California Highway Patrol officers are recovering from serious injuries after a Tesla hit their patrol car on I-80. The driver, 22, told investigators he was asleep and using FSD.
 Portland General Electric is promoting the benefits of switching heavy-duty haulage to electric, calling them batteries on wheels. Its promotion highlights the potential to support the grid.
 Huawei’s automotive unit Yinwang has just signed a new framework CATL and its battery swap subsidiary, giving it access to CATL’s battery swap network.
 BYD has submitted details of its third-generation Tang EV to China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The submission comes ahead of the car’s official launch later this year.
 Volkswagen has officially opened the order books for the ID. Cross with an entry-level 37 kWh battery In Germany, the model will retail from €27,995.
 Polestar and Oxford University have partnered to understand how performance affects the human body. Their pilot study combined vehicle telemetry, biological monitoring data, and interview responses from 12 drivers.
 As promised, BYD has officially launched its second-generation Seagull EV in China, sold elsewhere as the Dolphin Surf or Dolphin Mini. Higher trims get 5-minute flash charging.
 Xpeng’s CEO was in Paris this month, handing over the keys of the first L03s delivered in Europe. The company is pushing to become a volume brand in the region.
 CATL has unveiled a new Dual-Electric range-extending battery pack for electric trucks. It lets drivers use over 95% of the main swappable battery, up from around 70%.
 GM is closing its battery assembly plant in Brownstown, Michigan, south of Detroit. But it’s not for the reasons you might think: the facility’s lease is simply ending.
 Mercedes-Benz is bringing point-to-point Level 2 driving to Germany. MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO opens to early-access drivers in Stuttgart and Munich this year, with orders from 2027.
 Bolt has chosen Nvidia’s Alpamayo self-driving software for its planned European robotaxi fleet of Lucid EVs. Data collection starts in Madrid next year, without passengers.
 Despite not quite yet being available, Lexus has officially priced its 2027 Lexus TZ EV for the U.S. market. It will retail from $64,050, with all-wheel drive as standard.
 Japanese-based GreenTech company GSA has opened a new battery recycling lab in Switzerland. It will be used to further grow the company’s research into battery recycling.
 The Kia PV5 in 7-seat guise is now officially eligible for the UK Government’s Electric Car Grant program. It qualifies us for £1,500 off its sticker price, starting from £35,495 on the road.
 BYD’s Danza-branded EVs are now on sale in Indonesia, renamed locally following a trademark dispute over its usual name, Danza. 100 Flash chargers will also be installed nationwide.
 As Waymo reportedly targets 20,000 robotaxis by the end of 2027, the Alphabet-owned company is planning its first service in Canada, with a Toronto launch in 2028.
 And finally for the shorts, as oil prices soar, Scania is speeding up its electric truck plans, bringing forward Chinese production as operators seek a cheaper alternative to Diesel.
 And those are your news shorts — there will be more next week.
 Our final two stories are coming next, but first, a message from one of our most important channel sponsors – You!
 As one of the oldest and most independent YouTube channels in this space, we’ve spent over 16 years distilling cleaner, greener, safer, smarter and more equitable transportation and energy news into the information you need to make informed choices. We believe information should be free, and we don’t believe in handing over our opinions for money. And since YouTube is getting worse not better in the way it treats creators, it’s no longer a viable revenue stream – it’s just a delivery medium.
 And that means we have to rely on you for our income. We have a tiny team of myself and two full-time staff – and while we do make ends meet, it’s only just. So I’d love you to consider supporting us from $1.50 a month on Patreon or YouTube, or indeed buy swag from our swag store – like our brand-new Halloween and Mid-Term T-shirts for 2026! Pick between a Halloween EV1 being driven by a zombie Dino, or an electric eagle taking names at the ballot box. And if that isn’t your thing, you can also send us Ko-Fi, send us old-fashioned checks, or engage our team for Video Production or EV consultation work! Or you can just engage with and share our content – that really helps However you choose to support, it all helps! Thanks!
 And now it’s time for our final two stories.
 Ever since the U.S. Federal Government rolled back EV-supporting policies, the U.S. auto industry has become far less interested in EVs than it once was.
 And that’s had some big impacts on the EV sales charts. Tesla has sat at the top of the sales charts, for years, but second place has always been a toughly fought affair. But in Q3, second place was occupied by Rivian. After the brand began sales of its R2 SUV earlier this year, we’ve watched as its sales figures have ramped up. With its Rivian Adventure Network offering EV drivers cheaper charging than Tesla’s Superchargers – and without any of the associated bad-mouth tastes from supporting a guy whose reputation isn’t exactly the best – right now, I watched my video from Tuesday this week if you want to know more – Rivian is indeed cashing in. And with the R3 due in the near future, it’s showing no signs of slowing.
 And finally,
 in 2023, Vi and I had the pleasure of visiting Oxfordshire headquarters of Fortescue Zero (then known as Williams Advanced Engineering) and we got to see all the work it’d done on EV battery packs, from Formula E to massive mining trucks.
 And those batteries, are now in production 240-tonne mining vehicles built by Liebherr and put to work in Australia. They’re very large and powerful. To recharge them quickly requires a 6-megawatt charging cable that’s liquid-cooled. Imagine wrestling a charging cable several times larger into the charge port of a vehicle as tall as a two-storey house when compared to your EV. And that’s why Fortescue has developed a new robot whose sole purpose is to plug in and unplug these monsters of the mines. Working with KUKA, and with help from the Australian government, these robots make charging a breeze, avoiding worker strain and injury and recharging the Liebherr T264’s battery pack in just 30 minutes!
 And on that note, we’re done for today’s show.
